days.title: Historian Hysteria
days.approach: Parses the input into number pairs and unzips them into two lists. Part 1 sorts both and sums `diff` over the zipped pairs. Part 2 counts the right list and sums each left value times its count.
days.critique: Each part fits on one line, and `twoOf` with `unzip` keeps parsing compact. Sorting costs O(n log n), and the count map avoids a quadratic scan. Part 2 is hard to read: `counts <$> lists` counts only the right list via the tuple Functor, then `&<@>`, `<.>`, a flipped `|?` and `? 0` follow, and decoding it needs the prelude's signatures.
days.html: module Day1 (part1, part2) where lists :: [ℤ] × [ℤ] lists = $(aoc 1) |-.. twoOf (spaceTabs `surrounding` number) & unzip part1 :: ℤ part1 = Σ ˙ sort `both` lists ⤊ diff part2 :: ℤ part2 = Σ ˙ counts <$> lists &<@> (*) <.> ((⇄ (|?)) .>. (? 0))

days.title: Red-Nosed Reports
days.approach: A recursive parser reads numbers one at a time, prepending each to the accumulated list. With `skip` set, an alternative consumes one `anyWord` and continues with skipping disabled.
days.critique: The guard multiplies every difference by each distinct sign and requires all products to lie in [1,2,3], so mixed signs or a zero difference fail and one check enforces both direction and step size. Tolerance is just another `trying` alternative. `diffs` is recomputed over the whole accumulated list at each step rather than incrementally.
days.html: module Day2 (part1, part2) where safe :: 𝔹 -> [ℤ] -> Parser (Σ ℤ) safe skip ls = trying [ succeed (Σ 1), guard skip >> anyWord >> safe False ls, do (lss, ds) <- second diffs . dup . (: ls) <$> wordOf number guard (null ls || all (`elem` [1, 2, 3]) ((*) <$> ds <*> (nub (sgn <$> ds)))) safe skip lss ] part1 :: ℤ part1 = $(aoc 2) |-<..> safe False [] part2 :: ℤ part2 = $(aoc 2) |-<..> safe True []

days.title: Mull It Over
days.approach: A recursive parser tries ordered alternatives at each position: do() and don't() set an enabled flag, mul(a,b) yields a Σ of Π values, any other character is skipped, and |-<.> runs the parser on the input.
days.critique: One parser serves both parts. The first Bool is the state don't() switches to, so part 1 passes True and effectively ignores don't. A disabled mul still parses but produces Σ [Π 0] instead of being dropped, and the Σ/Π wrappers express the sum-of-products. The paired Bool parameters are cryptic, and the anyChar fallback means the parser advances one character at a time through junk input.
days.html: module Day3 (part1, part2) where muls :: 𝔹 -> 𝔹 -> Parser [Σ [Π ℤ]] muls dont on = let mul True = hom Σ $ cargs #mul (hdup number) mul False = mul True $> Σ [Π 0] in trying [ cfunc_ #do *> muls dont True, cfunc_ #don't *> muls dont dont, (:) <$> mul on <*> muls dont on, anyChar >> muls dont on, pure [] ] part1 :: ℤ part1 = $(aoc 3) |-<.> muls True True part2 :: ℤ part2 = $(aoc 3) |-<.> muls False True

days.title: Ceres Search
days.approach: Each Text argument is parsed with readGrid; every grid from its rotations list goes to convolveWith as the first argument, with the $(grid 4) splice second; result cells are folded into a Σ ℤ total via its Monoid instance.
days.critique: One function serves both parts: part 1 passes two text grids (a straight one and a diagonal one with '_' cells), part 2 one. Because rotations returns a list of same-typed grids, the applicative <$>/<*> yields one convolution per rotation and avoids per-direction code. The type-level arity (@n via variadicat) and the compile-time splice add machinery that makes the call sites harder to read.
days.html: module Day4 (part1, part2) where occurrences :: forall n. n -*=| Text |=*-> Σ ℤ occurrences = variadicat @n @Text $ \kernel -> cells |=< convolveWith (Σ . as @ℤ .<. x_x) <$> rotations (readGrid kernel) <*> pure ($(grid 4) :: HashGrid' (ℤ₆₄, ℤ₆₄) Char) part1 :: Σ ℤ part1 = occurrences @2 [txt|XMAS|] [txt|X___ _M__ __A_ ___S|] part2 :: Σ ℤ part2 = occurrences @1 [txt|M_S _A_ M_S|]

days.title: Print Queue
days.approach: Parses the `|` lines into a Map from each left-hand page to its right-hand pages, sorts each update with a comparator built from that map, and sums middle elements of unchanged (part 1) or reordered (part 2) updates.
days.critique: Sorting with the rule-derived comparator and comparing against the original lets one `solve` helper handle both parts. `mkCompare` only checks whether `b` is listed under `a`, so a pair with no rule either way gets GT in both orders, which is not a lawful ordering; the results rely on every pair in an update having a rule. Membership is a linear list scan. The local `solve` shadows quaalude's Z3 `solve`.
days.html: module Day5 (part1, part2) where (rules, orders) :: (Map ℤ [ℤ], [[ℤ]]) = $(aoc 5) |- ( (,) <$> (mapcat "|" number number <* eol) <*> (many1 ((number @ℤ `sepBy1` char ',') <* eol)) ) mkCompare :: Map ℤ [ℤ] -> ℤ -> ℤ -> Ordering mkCompare lt a b | a == b = EQ | b ∈ (lt |? a ? [b]) = LT | otherwise = GT solve :: ([ℤ] -> [ℤ] -> ℤ) -> ℤ solve f = sum (zipWith f orders (sortBy (mkCompare rules) <$> orders)) part1 :: ℤ part1 = solve (\a b -> bool 0 (middle a) (a == b)) part2 :: ℤ part2 = solve (\a b -> bool (middle b) 0 (a == b))

days.title: Guard Gallivant
days.approach: Simulates the guard with a Set of (position, direction) states, returning Nothing on a repeat. Part 2 reruns the walk with '#' at each visited position, counting Nothing results minus one.
days.critique: A single `walk` serves both parts, since a repeated (cell, direction) state means a loop. Part 2 reruns the whole simulation once per visited position. The fold starts at (-1) with no comment explaining the offset. The point-free `walk'`, built from `>>>` and `(+)`, is hard to read.
days.html: module Day6 (part1, part2) where walk :: Grid Char -> Ѓ (Set (ℤ₆₄ × ℤ₆₄)) (?) walk g = go (∅) def =<< (gridFindOne '^' g) where go seen d c | (c, d) ∈ seen = Nothing | c ∉ g = Just $ setMap fst seen | g |? move @ℤ₆₄ d 1 c == Just '#' = go seen (turnCW d) c | otherwise = go ((c, d) |-> seen) d (move @ℤ₆₄ d 1 c) part1 :: Ѓ ℤ (?) part1 = size <$> walk $(grid 6) part2 :: Ѓ ℤ (?) part2 = let g = $(grid 6) walk' = (((as @ℤ . isNothing . walk . (g ||.) . (,'#')) >>>) . (+)) in foldl' walk' (-1) <$> (unSet <$> walk g)

days.title: Bridge Repair
days.approach: Each line's numbers go through `snoc`; `f` recurses over the list with `0` as its other argument, expanding every operator via `(ops >>=)`, and `Σ t` is summed when `t` is a result.
days.critique: Passing the operator list into `with` lets both parts share one evaluator, with operator choices expanded by list-monad bind. It is brute force: all operator combinations are generated and membership of `t` is tested only at the end. Part 2's `||` builds `show a <> show b` and parses that string with `number`. The point-free composition in `f` is dense to read.
days.html: module Day7 (part1, part2) where with :: [ℤ -> ℤ -> ℤ] -> Parser (Σ ℤ) with ops = let f (x : xs) = (ops >>=) . ((f xs . ($ x)) .<. (&)) f [] = pure g t = bool (Σ 0) (Σ t) . (t ∈) . ((⇄ f) 0) in g <$@> snoc <$> numbers part1 :: Σ ℤ part1 = $(aoc 7) |-<..?!> with [(+), (*)] part2 :: Σ ℤ part2 = let a || b = number -| show a <> show b in $(aoc 7) |-<..?!> with [(+), (*), (||)]

days.title: Resonant Collinearity
days.approach: Converts the grid with `co` into a `Map Char` of positions, drops '.', forms all ordered position pairs per character via `join cartesian`, generates `b + (i,i)⋅(b-a)` over a range of i, deduplicates, and counts in-grid points.
days.critique: Both parts share `step`. Part 1 passes the fixed range [1..1]. Part 2 uses `$$@` to apply one grid value twice, once to derive a single global bound from `maxXY` and once as input. That bound exceeds what pairs with larger offsets need, so their extra points are discarded by the membership test. List `nub` is quadratic where a set would not be, and the point-free chain is hard to follow without quaalude's definitions.
days.html: module Day8 (part1, part2) where antinodes :: ℤ -> ℤ -> Map Char [ℤ × ℤ] -> [ℤ × ℤ] antinodes l u = let nodes (a, b) = (a ≡ b) ??? [b + (i, i) ⋅ (b - a) | i <- [l .. u]] $ [] in nub ∘ (>>= (>>= nodes) ∘ join cartesian) ∘ values ∘ (|/ '.') step :: ℤ -> ℤ -> Grid' (ℤ × ℤ) Char -> Σ ℤ step l u = (((as @(Σ ℤ) ∘ Σ) .<. (∋)) &<$>& (antinodes l u ∘ co)) <>∘ dup part1 :: Σ ℤ part1 = step 1 1 $ $(grid 8) part2 :: Σ ℤ part2 = step 0 ∘ (max $@) ∘ maxXY $$@ $(grid 8)

days.title: Disk Fragmenter
days.approach: After prepending '0', the input parses as (gap, file) length pairs. Gaps go into a min-priority queue keyed by start, and each file range is placed in the leftmost gap before it that fits.
days.critique: One function solves both parts. Files are fed last-first; part 1 splits each into single-block ranges, part 2 keeps whole ranges. Each range's checksum comes in closed form from triangular numbers. In place, too-small gaps before a file are popped and reinserted on the way back, so in part 2 one move can cost time linear in the earlier gaps. The point-free tuple pipeline (bimap, &@, $@, <:>, swap) is dense.
days.html: module Day9 (part1, part2) where defragment :: ([(ℤ, (ℤ, ℤ))] -> [(ℤ, (ℤ, ℤ))]) -> ℤ defragment by = ('0' : $(aoc 9)) |- many (twoOf (as @ℤ ∘ digitToInt <$> digit)) & (..#) & foldl' ( \(ends, files, start) (i, (free, full)) -> ( free > 0 ??? ends $ ends |. (start, start + free - 1), (i, (start + free, start + free + full - 1)) : files, start + free + full ) ) (ø, ø, 0) & (\(a, b, _) -> (a, b)) & (bimap (,0) by) &@ foldl' ( \(ends, score) (i, r) -> second ((+ score) ∘ (⋅ i) ∘ ((-) $@) ∘ (triangular <:>) ∘ second (subtract 1) ∘ swap) (place r ends) ) & snd where place r@(fa, fb) ends | nullQ ends = (ø, r) | a > fa = (ends' |. (a, b), r) | a - fa + fb ≡ b = (ends' |. r, (a, b)) | a - fa + fb < b = (ends' |. r |. (a - fa + fb + 1, b), (a, a - fa + fb)) | otherwise = first (|. (a, b)) (place r ends') where ((a, b), ends') = (ends <!) part1 :: ℤ part1 = defragment $ \files -> [(i, (block, block)) | (i, (a, b)) <- files, block <- [a .. b]] part2 :: ℤ part2 = defragment id

days.title: Hoof It
days.approach: From each height-0 cell, a queue search over a Seq follows 4-neighbours exactly one higher and collects reached 9s in a list. Part 1 nubs it; part 2 counts it.
days.critique: A skip flag and post-processing function let one traversal serve both parts. Part 2 never checks seen, so cells are re-expanded each time they are popped and work grows with trail count rather than grid size. Part 1 always passes skip=True, and the seen check runs before the 9 guard, so nines has no duplicates there and nub is redundant. The point-free chaining in hike is hard to read.
days.html: module Day10 (part1, part2) where trails :: 𝔹 -> G ℤ² ℕ₁₀ -> ℤ² -> [ℤ²] trails skip g c = let above c n = g |! n ≡ g |! c + 1 go (c :<| cs) seen nines | skip ∧ c ∈ seen = go cs seen nines | g |! c ≡ 9 = go cs (c |-> seen) (c : nines) | otherwise = go (cs >< (neighs @4 c g |-?-> above c)) (c |-> seen) nines go _ _ nines = nines in go (mk₁ c) ø ø hike :: ([ℤ²] -> [ℤ²]) -> 𝔹 -> Σ ℤ hike f skip = ($(grid 10) ⥢ (((Σ ∘ size ∘ f) ∘<∘ trails skip) &<$>& (|?> (0 :: ℕ₁₀))) <>!) part1 :: Σ ℤ part1 = hike nub True part2 :: Σ ℤ part2 = hike id False

days.title: Plutonian Pebbles
days.approach: Each parsed stone becomes an `Mℤ n S` key (blinks left, plus `S`, a `Dℤ`-wrapped digit sequence built by `mkS`). A memoised `blink` is traversed over all stones, and the joined result sequence's `size` is returned.
days.critique: Keeping digits as a sequence makes the even-length split a plain `halve` and the length test a `size` call. Memoising on (blinks left, stone) lets 75 blinks finish. But `blink` returns `Seq S`, concatenated with `(><)`, so memo entries hold stone sequences rather than counts. Results are counted only at the end with `size`. The `Mℤ`/`Dℤ` wrappers and `Dec` arithmetic obscure the rules.
days.html: module Day11 (part1, part2) where type S = Dℤ (Seq (ℕ₁₀)) mkS :: Seq ℕ₁₀ -> S mkS s = Dec @ℤ s ⋅ Dec (mk₁ 1) blink :: Mℤ S .->. Seq S blink (Mℤ 0 s) = return (mk₁ s) blink (Mℤ n (Dec (Seq₁ 0))) = blink .$. Mℤ (n - 1) (mkS (mk₁ 1)) blink (Mℤ n (Dec s)) | even (size s) = liftA2 (><) $@ both ((blink .$.) ∘ Mℤ (n - 1) ∘ mkS) (halve s) | otherwise = blink .$. Mℤ (n - 1) (Dec s * 2024) blinks :: ℤ -> ℤ blinks n = $(aoc 11) |- (mk <$> wordsOf (Mℤ n ∘ mkS ∘ mk <$> many1 nat₁₀)) & (size ∘ join ∘ run ∘ traverse blink) part1 :: ℤ part1 = blinks 25 part2 :: ℤ part2 = blinks 75

days.title: Garden Groups
days.approach: Repeatedly picks an unvisited cell and flood-fills its region with a Seq queue, accumulating area, perimeter and outward boundary segments, then counts sides by grouping segments by direction and splitting them into contiguous runs.
days.critique: One flood fill collects area, perimeter and boundary data. Keying segments by outward normal through `mkWith` keeps opposite edges of a thin strip apart, so a later sort and group finds straight runs. A cell can be enqueued several times before the membership guard skips it. The view-pattern guard and `<$@>` / `<>!` operators make the sides step hard to follow.
days.html: module Day12 (part1, part2) where region :: G ℤ² Char -> ℤ² -> (Set ℤ², ℤ, ℤ, Σ ℤ) region g c = let go r Empty segs area perim = (r, area, perim, sides segs) go r (((∈ r) -> True) :<| cs) segs area perim = go r cs segs area perim go r (c :<| cs) segs area perim = let ns = [n | n <- neighs @4 c g, g |! n ≡ g |! c] segs' = [(n - c, [c]) | n <- vicinity @4 c, g |? n /= g |? c] in go (c |-> r) (cs >< ns) (segs >< segs') (area + 1) (perim + 4 - size ns) sides segs = ((measure <$@> unMap (mkWith (<>) segs)) <>!) measure orientation cs = Σ . size $ case abs orientation of (0, 1) -> groupBy (\(x, y) (x', y') -> y ≡ y' ∧ diff x x' ≡ 1) (sortOn swap cs) (1, 0) -> groupBy (\(x, y) (x', y') -> x ≡ x' ∧ diff y y' ≡ 1) (sort cs) in go ø (mk₁ c) ø 0 0 prices :: G ℤ² Char -> ℤ² prices g = let go (null -> True) ps = ps go cs ps = let (r, area, perim, Σ sides) = region g (arbitrary cs) in go (cs \\ r) (bimap (+ area ⋅ perim) (+ area ⋅ sides) ps) in go (mk $ coords g) (0, 0) (part1, part2) :: (ℤ, ℤ) = prices $(grid 12)

days.title: Claw Contraption
days.approach: Runs gradient descent per machine on squared distance to the prize plus 3a+b, stepping by 0.001 times the gradient divided by ax and bx; stops on an exact hit or when the loss is unchanged from the previous step.
days.critique: Gradient descent is an unusual choice for a 2×2 linear system that Cramer's rule would solve exactly in constant time. Stopping when the loss equals the previous loss, or when the presses converted to integers hit the prize exactly, can miss solutions because of float error. The lens traversal adding 10^13 to indices 4 and 5 is compact. Any short final chunk from chunksOf 6 would crash the partial six-element match.
days.html: module Day13 (part1, part2) where descend :: ℝ -> ℝ² -> [ℝ] -> Σ ℤ descend last (a, b) claw@[ax, ay, bx, by, px, py] | l ≡ last = 0 | p (as @ℤ² (a, b)) ≡ as @ℤ² (px, py) = Σ (3 ⋅ (as @ℤ a) + (as @ℤ b)) | otherwise = descend l (a - (da / ax), b - (db / bx)) claw where p (a, b) = (a ⋅ as @ℤ ax + b ⋅ as @ℤ bx, a ⋅ as @ℤ ay + b ⋅ as @ℤ by) (dx, dy) = (\a b -> a ⋅ ax + b ⋅ bx - px, \a b -> a ⋅ ay + b ⋅ by - py) loss (a, b) = (dx a b) ** 2 + (dy a b) ** 2 + 3 * a + b grad (a, b) = ( 2 ⋅ (ax ⋅ (dx a b) + ay ⋅ (dy a b)) + 3, 2 ⋅ (bx ⋅ (dx a b) + by ⋅ (dy a b)) + 1 ) l = loss (a, b) (da, db) = both (* 0.001) (grad (a, b)) claws :: [[ℝ]] claws = $(aoc 13) |-..<> numbers & chunksOf 6 part1 :: Σ ℤ part1 = (claws <&> descend 0 (0, 0) <>!) part2 :: Σ ℤ part2 = ( claws & (mapped ∘ traversed ∘ indices (∈ [4 :: ℤ₆₄, 5])) +~ 10000000000000 <&> descend 0 (0, 0) <>! )

days.title: Restroom Redoubt
days.approach: Simulates robots with modular wraparound, counts quadrants after 100 steps, then iterates until successive symmetric KL divergences of the robots' x+y histogram against the grid's differ by at least 0.6.
days.critique: Part 2 projects robots onto anti-diagonals and measures symmetric KL divergence against the trapezoidal x+y distribution of all grid cells, so a large change between consecutive steps flags the clustered picture without image heuristics. The 0.6 threshold and the 101x103 dimensions are hard-coded constants. Using a list as a four-counter accumulator is less clear than a tuple, and logBase (exp 1) is a roundabout natural log.
days.html: module Day14 (part1, part2) where (dims@(w, h), robots) :: (ℤ², [ℤ⁴]) = ((101, 103), $(aoc 14) |-. tuples @4 (numbers @ℤ)) step :: ℤ⁴ -> ℤ⁴ step (x, y, vx, vy) = ((x + vx) `mod` w, (y + vy) `mod` h, vx, vy) part1 :: ℤ part1 = product $ foldl' ( \[ul, ur, dl, dr] (x, y) -> case (x < w `div` 2, y < h `div` 2) of (True, True) -> [ul + 1, ur, dl, dr] (True, False) -> [ul, ur, dl + 1, dr] (False, True) -> [ul, ur + 1, dl, dr] (False, False) -> [ul, ur, dl, dr + 1] ) [0, 0, 0, 0] [ (x, y) | (x, y, _, _) <- foldl' (\rs _ -> step <$> rs) robots [1 .. 100], (∧) $@ bimap (x ≢) (y ≢) (both (`div` 2) dims) ] findTree :: ℝ -> Map ℤ ℝ -> ℝ -> ℝ -> ℤ -> [ℤ⁴] -> ℤ findTree threshold q qn kl n rs = let kl' = kl0 q qn rs in if diff kl kl' >= threshold then n else findTree threshold q qn kl' (n + 1) (step <$> rs) kl0 :: Map ℤ ℝ -> ℝ -> [ℤ⁴] -> ℝ kl0 q qn rs = let p = as @ℝ @ℤ <$> counts [x + y | (x, y, _, _) <- rs] pn = as @ℝ $ length rs in sum [ kl px pn qx qn + kl qx qn px pn | (d, px) <- unMap p, let qx = q |! d, qx ≢ 0, let kl ax an bx bn = (ax / an) ⋅ logBase (exp 1) (bn ⋅ ax / an ⋅ bx) ] part2 :: ℤ part2 = let q = as @ℝ @ℤ <$> counts [x + y | x <- [0 .. w - 1], y <- [0 .. h - 1]] qn = w ⋅ h in findTree 0.6 q (qn & as @ℝ) (kl0 q (qn & as @ℝ) robots) 0 robots

days.title: Warehouse Woes
days.approach: Simulates the robot on a grid, recursively collecting the layer of box cells each push reaches until hitting walls or empty space, then applying the resulting list of grid-update functions to the grid.
days.critique: One `step` handles both parts: `affected` adds the partner half only for vertical pushes of `[`/`]`, and `nub` stops a shared box being pushed twice. Each layer's move is a partially applied `movs` (`flip $ foldl' ...`) waiting for the grid; `foldl' (&) g moves` applies them farthest layer first, a compact but indirect encoding. `wide` omits `OL`/`OR`, safe only because they never appear before widening.
days.html: module Day15 (part1, part2) where data C = W | S | O | R | OL | OR deriving (Eq, Show, Ord) instance GridCell C where cs = [(W, '#'), (S, '.'), (O, 'O'), (R, '@'), (OL, '['), (OR, ']')] gps :: ℤ² -> Σ ℤ gps (x, y) = Σ (100 ⋅ y + x) step :: [Dir²] -> ℤ² -> G ℤ² C -> G ℤ² C step [] _ g = g step (dir : dirs) robot g = case (g |! robot', push [robot]) of (S, _) -> step dirs robot' (g |. (robot, S) |. (robot', R)) (W, _) -> step dirs robot g (_, Just moves) -> step dirs robot' (foldl' (&) g moves) _ -> step dirs robot g where robot' = move @ℤ dir 1 robot push cs = let cs' = move @ℤ dir 1 <$> cs movs = flip $ foldl' (\g c -> g |. (c, S) |. (move @ℤ dir 1 c, g |! c)) affected = nub $ mconcat $ [ case (g |! c, dir) of (O, _) -> [c] (OL, DirUp) -> [c, (x + 1, y)] (OL, DirDown) -> [c, (x + 1, y)] (OR, DirUp) -> [c, (x - 1, y)] (OR, DirDown) -> [c, (x - 1, y)] (_, DirRight) -> [c] (_, DirLeft) -> [c] _ -> [] | c@(x, y) <- cs' ] affected' = (g |!) ∘ move @ℤ dir 1 <$> affected in if | any (≡ W) affected' -> Nothing | all (≡ S) affected' -> Just $ [movs affected] <> [movs cs] | otherwise -> (<>) <$> push affected <*> Just [movs cs] widen :: G ℤ² C -> G ℤ² C widen g = mkGrid [ c | ((x, y), v) <- unGrid g, let (l, r) = wide v, c <- [((2 ⋅ x, y), l), ((2 ⋅ x + 1, y), r)] ] where wide R = (R, S) wide O = (OL, OR) wide W = (W, W) wide S = (S, S) sim :: (G ℤ² C -> G ℤ² C) -> C -> Σ ℤ sim f o = let (g, dirs) = $(aoc 15) |- ( (,) <$> (f <$> (readGrid @G @ℤ² @C ∘ pack <$> manyOf "#.O@\n")) <*> (fromArrow2 <$$> (mconcat <$> (linesOf (manyOf "<>^v") <* eof))) ) in (step dirs (g |!> R) g |?> o <&> gps <>!) part1 :: Σ ℤ part1 = sim id O part2 :: Σ ℤ part2 = sim widen OL

days.title: Reindeer Maze
days.approach: Compresses the maze into a graph of junctions joined by straight corridors that store their tile sets, then runs a priority-queue search ordered by cost plus a turn-and-distance estimate over (position, facing) states carrying accumulated tiles.
days.critique: Storing corridor tiles on edges keeps the graph small, and the finished routes' tile sets are unioned once at the end, so no backtracking pass is needed. The seen map keeps the first cost popped per state and drops other costs, so part 2 relies on the estimate in `h` never popping a state above its optimal cost. Each queued state copies a Set, and `foldl1` is partial if no route exists.
days.html: module Day16 (part1, part2) where -- [grid|#.ES|] data C = Wall | Space | Start | End deriving (Show, Eq, Ord) instance GridCell C where cs = [(Wall, '#'), (Space, '.'), (Start, 'S'), (End, 'E')] graph :: G ℤ² C -> Map ℤ² (Map ℤ² (Dir², Set ℤ²)) graph g = go (mk₁ (g |!> Start)) ø where nds c = [c `goingTo` n | n <- vicinity @4 c, g |! n ≢ Wall] straight path c d | size path > 0 ∧ isNode c = (c, path) | otherwise = let c' = move @ℤ d 1 c in case g |! c' of Wall -> (c, path) _ -> straight (c |-> path) c' d isNode c = case nds c of [[d], [d']] -> d ≢ opposite @Dir² d' _ -> True go Empty gr = gr go (c :<| q) gr | c ∈ gr = go q gr | otherwise = let nodes = [(c', (d, line)) | d <- (enumerate @Dir²), let (c', line) = straight ø c d, c ≢ c'] in go (q >< mk (fst <$> nodes)) (gr |. (c, mkMap nodes)) paths :: ℤ² -> ℤ² -> Map ℤ² (Map ℤ² (Dir², Set ℤ²)) -> (ℤ, ℤ) paths start end gr = go (ꝏ @ℤ) (mkQ₁ h (start, DirRight, 0, ø)) [] ø where score n x t = n + x + 1000 ⋅ t h (c, facing, n, _) = score n (manhattan c end) (maximum (0 : [turnDiff d facing | d <- c `goingTo` end])) go cap ((c, facing, n, path) :<!! q) paths (seen :: Map (ℤ², Dir²) ℤ) | n > cap = (cap, size (foldl1 (∪) paths)) | c ≡ end = go n q ((end |-> path) : paths) (seen |. ((c, facing), n)) | (c, facing) ∈ seen ∧ seen |! (c, facing) ≢ n = go cap q paths seen | otherwise = let st (c', (facing', path')) = ( c', facing', score n (size path') (turnDiff facing facing'), path' ∪ path ) ins q next = qInsert h (st next) q in go cap (foldl' ins q (unMap (gr |! c))) paths (seen |. ((c, facing), n)) (part1, part2) :: (ℤ, ℤ) = let (g :: G ℤ² C) = $(grid 16) in paths (g |!> Start) (g |!> End) (graph g)

days.title: Chronospatial Computer
days.approach: f₁ is a hard-coded formula giving one output digit from register A. Part 1's f shifts A right three bits per digit; part 2's allA rebuilds A three bits at a time from the last digit backwards.
days.critique: allA extends each candidate by eight 3-bit suffixes, keeps those whose f₁ output matches the next digit, explores every surviving branch through list-monad bind and takes the minimum. f₁ hard-codes one specific program (xor constants 3 and 5), and the parsed program serves only as part 2's target without ever being interpreted. The precedence-dependent one-liner in f₁ is hard to read.
days.html: module Day17 (part1, part2) where f :: ℤ -> Seq ℕ₈ f 0 = mkSeq [] f a = f₁ a <| f (a `div` 8) f₁ :: ℤ -> ℕ₈ f₁ a = let b = a `mod` 8 `xor` 3 in as @ℕ₈ $ b `xor` a `div` 2 ^ b `xor` 5 `mod` 8 allA :: Seq ℕ₈ -> ℤ -> [ℤ] allA Empty a = [a] allA (ns :|> n) a = allA ns =<< [a' | a' <- [8 ⋅ a .. 8 ⋅ a + 7], f₁ a' ≡ n] (part1, part2) :: (String, ℤ) = $(aoc 17) |- (numbers @ℤ <&> (bimap (fst3 ∘ toTup @3) (mkSeq . fmap (as @ℕ₈)) ∘ splitAt 3)) & bimap (intercalate "," ∘ fmap show ∘ un ∘ f) (minimum ∘ flip allA 0)

days.title: RAM Run
days.approach: scanl' builds one grid per prefix of falling bytes. A* ordered by steps plus Manhattan distance returns the reversed path to the goal, whose size answers part 1. Part 2 searches for the first unreachable index.
days.critique: Precomputing all prefix grids lets `paths n` fetch grid `n + 1` directly, but each searchFromTo probe still runs a full A*. `path` accepts a step-indexed vector of grids, yet callers wrap one grid in `pure`, so the `min` clamp is dead generality. The `n + 1` and `? -1` offsets are hard to verify, and 70 and 1024 are hard-coded.
days.html: module Day18 (part1, part2) where gs :: ℤ² -> Vector ℤ² -> Vector (G ℤ² Char) gs (w, h) = mk ∘ (scanl' ((∘ (,'#')) ∘ (|.))) (defGrid [(x, y) | x <- [0 .. w], y <- [0 .. h]]) ∘ un path :: ℤ² -> Vector (G ℤ² Char) -> [ℤ²] path dims gs = go (mkQ₁ h ((0, 0), 0, [])) (mkSet []) where g t = gs !! (min (t + 1) (size gs - 1)) h (c, t, _) = t + manhattan c dims go NullQ _ = [] go ((c, t, p) :<!! q) seen | c ≡ dims = p | not (cellEmpty c (g t)) ∨ c ∈ seen = go q seen | otherwise = let ns = neighs @4 @[] c (g t) in go (foldr (qInsert h ∘ (,t + 1,c : p)) q ns) (c |-> seen) (part1, part2) :: (ℤ, String) = let (dims, bytes) = ((70, 70), mk $ $(aoc 18) |- tuples @2 (numbers @ℤ)) gs' = gs dims bytes paths n = path dims (pure (gs' !! (n + 1))) in ( size (paths 1024), ((<>) $@) ∘ first (<> ",") ∘ both show $ (bytes !! ((searchFromTo (null ∘ paths) 1025 (size bytes - 1)) ? -1)) )

days.title: Linen Layout
days.approach: A memoised recursion counts the ways each design can be built by stripping towel prefixes. Each count n becomes the pair (signum n, n), and the pairs are monoid-summed to give both parts.
days.critique: The (signum, count) pair under the Σ monoid answers both parts in one pass. The .=<<. memo combinator keeps the recursion close to the recurrence, with the empty design as base case. Nearly every token is a custom operator or point-free composition, so the data flow is hard to follow without quaalude.
days.html: module Day19 (part1, part2) where (part1, part2) :: (Σ ℤ, Σ ℤ) = let go t p = p ≡ ø ??? go t .=<<. (stripPrefix <$> splitOn ", " t <*> [p] <>?) $ (Σ 1 #) in ((⥢ ((±) ⇱)) ∘ run ∘<∘ go &<$> snoc (flines $(aoc 19)) <>!)

days.title: Race Condition
days.approach: Walks the corridor from S to E by repeatedly taking the single unvisited open neighbour, indexes each path cell by its distance from E, then pairs each cell with every cell nearer E within the cheat's Manhattan radius.
days.critique: The `let [n] = ...` pattern assumes exactly one open unvisited neighbour at each step and crashes otherwise. The pair scan is O(N²) over path cells, with no spatial pruning. `size path - cost` is the true saving plus one, so the test also accepts savings of `threshold - 1`; the code alone does not rule out such cases.
days.html: module Day20 (part1, part2) where cheats :: ".#SE" ▦ ℤ² -> ℤ -> ℤ -> [Σ ℤ] cheats g duration threshold = [ Σ 1 | let path = go (g |!> (#E □)) [g |!> (#S □)] ø, let c2n = mkMap (zip path [0 ..]), (d, c) <- zip [0 ..] (reverse path), n <- drop (d + 1) (reverse path), let d' = manhattan c n, d' <= duration, let cost = d + d' + c2n |! n, size path - cost >= threshold ] where go end (c : cs) seen | c ≡ end = c : cs | otherwise = let [n] = [n | n <- neighs @4 c g, g |! n ≢ (#"#" □), n ∉ seen] in go end (n : c : cs) (c |-> seen) part1 :: Σ ℤ part1 = (cheats (readGrid $(aoc 20)) 2 100 <>!) part2 :: Σ ℤ part2 = (cheats (readGrid $(aoc 20)) 20 100 <>!)

days.title: Keypad Conundrum
days.approach: A queue-driven search records every neighbour walk between keys up to a length cap, then keeps all tied shortest walks per key pair. A memoised recursion picks the cheapest candidate, costing each move at the next layer.
days.critique: Memoising the inner `go'` on (layer, path) through `.$.` makes 25 layers cheap. Keeping every tied shortest path avoids hard-coding a move order. The search does not stop at the first shortest walks. It collects every gap-avoiding walk under the rows+cols−1 cap, including back-and-forth ones, then sorts, wasting work on tiny pads. Type-level keypad alphabets add machinery.
days.html: module Day21 where type NumPad = ".A0123456789" type DirPad = ".A^v<>" numPad :: NumPad ▦ ℤ² numPad = readGrid "789\n456\n123\n.0A" dirPad :: DirPad ▦ ℤ² dirPad = readGrid ".^A\n<v>" type Paths cs = (Cell cs, Cell cs) :|-> [[Cell DirPad]] paths :: (SChar '.' :< SymSChars cs, Ord (Cell cs), GridCell (Cell cs)) => cs ▦ ℤ² -> Paths cs paths g = shortest ∘ sortOn size <$> go (mk [(s, s, []) | s <- coords g]) where shortest ps@(p : _) = takeWhile ((≡ size p) ∘ size) ps go Empty = mkMap [((c, d), []) | c <- cells g, d <- cells g] go ((s, c, dirs) :<| q) | g |! c ≡ (#"." □) = go q | size dirs >= ((+) $@ gridDims g) - 1 = go q | otherwise = let ns = [(s, n, dirs <> (fromChar ∘ toArrow² <$> goingTo c n)) | n <- neighs @4 c g] in go (q >< mk ns) |~ ((g |! s, g |! c), (dirs :)) (numPaths, dirPaths) :: (Paths NumPad, Paths DirPad) = (paths numPad, paths dirPad) presses :: ℤ -> Cell NumPad -> Cell NumPad -> MM (ℤ, [Cell DirPad]) (Σ ℤ) presses layers = go numPaths 0 where go :: (Ord (Cell cs)) => Paths cs -> ℤ -> Cell cs -> Cell cs -> MM (ℤ, [Cell DirPad]) (Σ ℤ) go paths layer from to = minimum <$> forM (paths |! (from, to)) (\path -> go' .$. (layer, (path <> [(#A □)]))) go' ((≡ layers) -> True, path) = return ∘ Σ $ size path go' (layer, path) = sum <$> forM (zip ((#A □) : path) path) (&@ go dirPaths (layer + 1)) complexity :: ℤ -> Text -> Σ ℤ complexity layers code = let cs = unpack code bs = fromChar <$> cs value = Σ $ take 3 cs |- number go start b = run (presses layers start b) in value ⋅ fst (foldl' (\(ps, start) b -> (ps + go start b, b)) (Σ 0, (#A □)) bs) part1 :: Σ ℤ part1 = (complexity 2 <$> (lines $(aoc 21)) <>!) part2 :: Σ ℤ part2 = (complexity 25 <$> (lines $(aoc 21)) <>!)

days.title: Monkey Market
days.approach: Part 1 iterates the shift/xor/prune step with scanl'. Part 2 maps each four-change window to its price per buyer via mkMap over the reversed window list, then tries every distinct window across all buyers.
days.critique: Reversing before mkMap appears meant to make the earliest occurrence win, assuming mkMap keeps the last duplicate as Data.Map.fromList does. Part 2 is slow: an Eq-only nub over every buyer's keys is quadratic in the number of windows, and each candidate is then looked up in every buyer's map. Merging the per-buyer maps with a summing union would avoid both.
days.html: module Day22 (part1, part2) where secret :: ℤ -> ℤ secret s0 = s3 where prune = (`mod` 16777216) s1 = prune $ (s0 ⋅ 64) `xor` s0 s2 = prune $ (s1 `div` 32) `xor` s1 s3 = prune $ (s2 ⋅ 2048) `xor` s2 secrets :: ℤ -> ℤ -> NonEmpty ℤ³ secrets n x = let (s : ss) = scanl' ( \(s, s₁, _) _ -> let s' = secret s s'₁ = decDigit 1 s' in (s', s'₁, s'₁ - s₁) ) (x, decDigit 1 x, ꝏ) [1 .. n] in s :| ss prices :: NonEmpty ℤ³ -> ℤ⁴ :|-> ℤ prices = let go ((_, _, a₁) :| b@(_, _, b₁) : c@(_, _, c₁) : d@(_, price, d₁) : xs) = ((a₁, b₁, c₁, d₁), price) : go (b :| c : d : xs) go _ = [] in mkMap ∘ reverse ∘ go part1 :: Σ ℤ part1 = ($(aoc 22) |- numbers @ℤ <&> Σ ∘ fst3 ∘ last ∘ secrets 2000 <>!) part2 :: Σ ℤ part2 = let pms = $(aoc 22) |- numbers @ℤ <&> prices ∘ secrets 2000 in maximum [ ([Σ (pm |? seq ? 0) | pm <- pms] <>!) | seq <- nub (keys <$> pms <>!) ]

days.title: LAN Party
days.approach: Builds a symmetric adjacency map, then grows cliques level by level, extending each by every vertex adjacent to all members; part 1 filters 3-cliques, part 2 takes the last level.
days.critique: Each level is a Set of Sets, so permutations collapse and the scanl' yields each clique once, with both parts reusing one list. Growth is brute force: every clique is tested against every vertex each round. The `where` binding `(cl : cls)` is a refutable list pattern that would fail at runtime on an empty graph, and `clique !! 2` relies on index 2 being the 3-clique level.
days.html: module Day23 (part1, part2) where clique :: NonEmpty (Set (Set String)) clique = cliques $ mk <$> mkWith (∪) ( [ [(a, mk₁ b), (b, mk₁ a)] | (a, bs) <- unMap ($(aoc 23) |- (mapcat "-" abc abc)), b <- bs ] <>! ) cliques :: (String :|-> Set String) -> NonEmpty (Set (Set String)) cliques g = cl :| cls where expand cs = mk [ c |-> cs | c <- keys g, all ((c ∈) ∘ (g |!)) cs ] (cl : cls) = takeWhile (not ∘ null) $ scanl' (\cs _ -> setConcatMap expand cs) (mk (mk₁ <$> keys g)) [0 .. size g] part1 :: Σ ℤ part1 = ( [ Σ 1 | [x : _, y : _, z : _] <- un <$> un (clique !! (2 :: ℤ)), 't' ∈ [x, y, z] ] <>! ) part2 :: String part2 = intercalate "," ∘ sort ∘ un ∘ setConcat ∘ last $ clique

days.title: Crossed Wires
days.approach: Part 1 recursively evaluates every z wire over the gate map. Part 2 builds expression trees for all circuit keys, diffs them against a generated ripple-carry adder, and records swaps recursively until the adder matches or eight entries exist.
days.critique: Comparing trees with commutative matching (diffTree) against a reference adder finds swaps structurally, not by brute force. Wire evaluation is unmemoised, and each fixAdd call re-parses the input. The nested let pattern is refutable and fails if getclosest returns nothing. swaptext and treeIn (which has a duplicated clause) are never called by part1 or part2, the local !+! is unused, and traceShow calls remain in part2's path.
days.html: module Day24 where import Control.Applicative qualified as CA import Data.Bimap qualified as BM import Data.Text qualified as T import Text.Show qualified as TS swaptext = T.unpack ∘ T.replace "vmr XOR bnc -> hmk" "vmr XOR bnc -> z16" ∘ T.replace "y16 AND x16 -> z16" "y16 AND x16 -> hmk" ∘ T.replace "pns AND tsc -> z20" "pns AND tsc -> fhp" ∘ T.replace "tsc XOR pns -> fhp" "tsc XOR pns -> z20" ∘ T.replace "x27 AND y27 -> rvf" "x27 AND y27 -> tpc" ∘ T.replace "y27 XOR x27 -> tpc" "y27 XOR x27 -> rvf" ∘ T.replace "wkw OR jgr -> z33" "wkw OR jgr -> fcd" ∘ T.replace "smf XOR rfd -> fcd" "smf XOR rfd -> z33" ∘ T.pack inp :: (String -> String) -> (Map String 𝔹, Map String (String, String, String)) inp swaps = $(aoc 24) |- ( (,) <$> ((mapSep (string ": ") eol abc123 (as @𝔹 <$> number @ℤ)) <* eol) <*> ((\m -> mkWith (<>) [(swaps w, op) | (op, ws) <- unMap m, w <- ws]) <$> (mapcat "-> " (tuple @3 (abcABC123 <* spaces)) abc123)) ) value :: Map String 𝔹 -> Map String String -> Map String (String, String, String) -> String -> 𝔹 value initial swap' circuit w' | w ∈ initial = initial |! w | otherwise = let v = value initial swap' circuit in case circuit |! w of (w, "AND", y) -> v w ∧ v y (w, "OR", y) -> v w ∨ v y (w, "XOR", y) -> v w `xor` v y where w = case swap' |? w' of Nothing -> w' Just w -> w to :: ℤ -> Char -> ℤ -> Map String 𝔹 to n c x = mkMap [ (c : pad 2 '0' (show i), b) | (i, b) <- zip [n - 1, n - 2 ..] (pad (as @ℤ₆₄ n) False (intToBits (as @ℤ₆₄ x))) ] go :: Map String 𝔹 -> Map String String -> Map String (String, String, String) -> ℤ go initial swap' circuit = bitsToInt $ snd <$> sortOn (Down ∘ fst) [ (n |- number @ℤ, value initial swap' circuit w) | w@(z : n) <- keys circuit, z ≡ 'z' ] part1 :: ℤ part1 = let (xy, circuit) = inp id in go xy ø circuit indent :: Int -> String -> String indent n s = unpack (unlines ((pack (replicate n ' ') <>) <$> lines (pack s))) data Circuit = OR Circuit Circuit | AND Circuit Circuit | XOR Circuit Circuit | N String deriving (Eq, Ord) part2 :: String part2 = intercalate "," (sort (keys (fixAdd mempty ? mempty))) where fixAdd :: String :|-> String -> Maybe (String :|-> String) fixAdd swaps | size swaps ≡ 8 = Just swaps | size swaps > 8 = Nothing | otherwise = let f z = swaps |? z ? z circuit = snd (inp f) x !+! y = go (to n 'x' x <> to n 'y' y) (mkMap []) circuit m' :: BM.Bimap String (Maybe Circuit) m' = mkBimap [(z, getTree circuit z) | z <- keys circuit] m :: BM.Bimap String Circuit m = (? (N "()")) `BM.mapR` m' n = 1 + maximum [n |- number @ℤ | (z : n) <- keys circuit, z ≡ 'z'] x i = N ('x' : pad 2 '0' (show i)) y i = N ('y' : pad 2 '0' (show i)) z i = ('z' : pad 2 '0' (show i)) halfadd a b = (XOR a b, AND a b) add1 a b c = let (p, c0) = halfadd a b (s, c1) = halfadd p c in (s, OR c0 c1) cin 0 = N "()" cin 1 = AND (x 0) (y 0) cin i = snd $ add1 (x (i - 1)) (y (i - 1)) (cin (i - 1)) radd 0 = XOR (x 0) (y 0) radd i = fst $ add1 (x i) (y i) (cin i) diffit i = (diffTree (m BM.! (z i)) (radd i)) diffc i name = (diffTree (m BM.! name) (cin i)) real i = m BM.! (c1, c0)) e -> traceShow ("no match", e) $ Nothing -- instance TS.Show Circuit where -- show (OR a b) = "OR\n" <> indent 1 (show a <> "\n" <> show b) -- show (XOR a b) = "XOR\n" <> indent 1 (show a <> "\n" <> show b) -- show (AND a b) = "AND\n" <> indent 1 (show a <> "\n" <> show b) -- show (N a) = a instance TS.Show Circuit where show (OR a b) = "(OR " <> show a <> " " <> show b <> ")" show (XOR a b) = "(XOR " <> show a <> " " <> show b <> ")" show (AND a b) = "(AND " <> show a <> " " <> show b <> ")" show (N a) = a getTree :: String :|-> (String, String, String) -> String -> Maybe Circuit getTree cr = go mempty where go seen z | z ∈ seen = Nothing | otherwise = let seen' = z |-> seen in case cr |? z of Just (w, "AND", y) -> AND <$> go seen' w <*> go seen' y Just (w, "OR", y) -> OR <$> go seen' w <*> go seen' y Just (w, "XOR", y) -> XOR <$> go seen' w <*> go seen' y Nothing -> Just $ N z _ -> Nothing oneDs [] [] = [] oneDs a [] = [] oneDs [] b = [] oneDs a b = a diffTree :: Circuit -> Circuit -> [(Circuit, Circuit)] diffTree a b = go a b where go :: Circuit -> Circuit -> [(Circuit, Circuit)] go (AND a b) (AND a' b') = oneDs (go a a') (go a b') <> oneDs (go b b') (go b a') go (OR a b) (OR a' b') = oneDs (go a a') (go a b') <> oneDs (go b b') (go b a') go (XOR a b) (XOR a' b') = oneDs (go a a') (go a b') <> oneDs (go b b') (go b a') go (N a) (N b) | a ≡ b = [] | otherwise = [(N a, N b)] go a b = [(a, b)] treeIn t t'@(AND a b) = (diffTree t t' ≡ []) ∨ (treeIn t a) ∨ (treeIn t b) treeIn t t'@(OR a b) = (diffTree t t' ≡ []) ∨ (treeIn t a) ∨ (treeIn t b) treeIn t t'@(XOR a b) = (diffTree t t' ≡ []) ∨ (treeIn t a) ∨ (treeIn t b) treeIn t t'@(XOR a b) = (diffTree t t' ≡ []) ∨ (treeIn t a) ∨ (treeIn t b) treeIn t t' = diffTree t t' ≡ [] -- divs = [(fst <$> getclosest da, fst <$> getclosest db) | i <- [0 .. 44], let d = diffit i, not (null d), (da, db) <- d] -- prs = (catMaybes . (\(a, b) -> [a !? 0, b !? 0]) <$> divs) & filter ((== 2) . size) & fmap sort & sort & nub

days.title: Code Chronicle
days.approach: Parses all schematics into typed grids, forms pairs with triPairs, and counts a pair when the cell pair ('#','#') is absent from the zip of the two grids' cell lists, casting Bool to ℤ and summing.
days.critique: The overlap test is one expression: `dup` of the '#' cell checked with `∉` against the zipped cells. It never computes column heights or separates locks from keys. Correctness assumes the cell lists line up position by position, since `zip` truncates silently and this file has no size check. Every pair is compared directly, and the operator-heavy quaalude style is hard to read without the library.
days.html: module Day25 (part1, part2) where part1 :: Σ ℤ part1 = let (gs :: [".#" ▦ ℤ²]) = gridsT @Text $(aoc 25) f g g' = Σ ∘ as @ℤ $ (dup (#"#" □)) ∉ zip (cells g) (cells g') in ((f <$@> triPairs gs) <>!) part2 :: Text part2 = "Merry Christmas!"
